title: Processes vs Threads & Process Memory Layout
desc: The process/thread distinction, virtual address space layout (text, data, BSS, heap, stack), what is shared and what is private between threads, and how the OS creates and tears down each.

title: Process Control: fork, exec, wait, signals
desc: fork/exec/wait semantics, copy-on-write, orphans and zombies, signal delivery and handling, and async-signal-safety, all grounded in POSIX.

title: POSIX Threads: Creation, Joining & Attributes
desc: pthread_create/join/detach, thread attributes (stack size, detach state, scheduling), thread-local storage, and passing arguments and return values correctly.

title: Mutexes & Critical Sections
desc: pthread_mutex semantics, mutex types (normal, recursive, error-checking), spinlocks versus mutexes, critical section design, and real deadlock and contention code.

title: Condition Variables & Signaling
desc: pthread_cond_wait/signal/broadcast, the mandatory predicate-and-mutex pattern, lost wakeups and spurious wakeups, and building a bounded queue from a mutex and condition variable.

title: Semaphores, Read-Write Locks & Barriers
desc: POSIX semaphores versus mutexes, counting semaphores for resource pools, reader-writer locks and writer starvation, and thread barriers, each with real code.

title: Memory Model, Atomics & Ordering
desc: The C11 memory model, stdatomic.h, memory_order variants, compiler and hardware reordering, false sharing, and why volatile is not a substitute for atomics or locks.

title: Deadlock, Livelock, Starvation & Priority Inversion
desc: The four deadlock conditions, lock ordering and hierarchy, timeout- and try-lock-based avoidance, livelock and starvation scenarios, and priority inversion with the priority-inheritance fix.

title: Classic Concurrency Problems
desc: Producer-consumer, the readers-writers problem, and the dining philosophers, each implemented with real pthreads code and a discussion of the fairness and correctness trade-offs.

title: Thread-Safety Patterns & Lock-Free Basics
desc: Reentrancy versus thread-safety, thread-local storage, double-checked locking done correctly, compare-and-swap, and the limits of lock-free code for an application engineer to know.

title: OS Scheduling & Real-Time Concurrency
desc: Preemptive scheduling basics, scheduling classes (SCHED_OTHER/FIFO/RR), priorities and nice values, context-switch cost, and what changes when code must meet a real-time deadline.

title: Inter-Process Communication
desc: Pipes and named pipes, POSIX message queues, shared memory with synchronization, and signals as a control-plane IPC mechanism, contrasted with in-process threading.

title: Virtual Memory & mmap
desc: Paging and page faults, mmap for files and anonymous memory, shared versus private mappings, memory-mapped I/O in firmware, and how the MMU underlies everything in modules 1 and 7.

title: Interrupts, ISRs & Embedded Concurrency
desc: Interrupt context versus thread/task context, why an ISR cannot block, disabling interrupts versus locking, top-half/bottom-half style splits, and reentrancy in interrupt-driven firmware.

title: Debugging Concurrency & Principal-Level Design
desc: Finding races with ThreadSanitizer/helgrind, reasoning about a hang or a rare corruption, and Principal-level design questions: a thread pool, a deadlock-free multi-lock ordering scheme, and a bounded blocking queue built from first principles.
